about_blocks.text: Pine River Institute: Live-In Treatment for Youth 13 to 19 near Shelburne, Ontario
about_blocks.html: Pine River Institute: Live-In Treatment for Youth 13 to 19 near Shelburne, Ontario

about_blocks.text: Pine River Institute is a not-for-profit, live-in treatment centre for young people aged 13 to 19 who are struggling with addictive behaviours, and often with other mental health problems as well. The campus sits on 200 acres just outside Shelburne, in the Township of Mulmur, roughly 100 km northwest of Toronto. The program opened in 2006 and is run as a registered charity.
about_blocks.html: Pine River Institute is a not-for-profit, live-in treatment centre for young people aged 13 to 19 who are struggling with addictive behaviours, and often with other mental health problems as well. The campus sits on 200 acres just outside Shelburne, in the Township of Mulmur, roughly 100 km northwest of Toronto. The program opened in 2006 and is run as a registered charity.

about_blocks.text: Most families come to Pine River after other help has not worked. The centre says the teens it sees are usually struggling on several fronts at once: substance use, self-harm or disordered eating, anxiety or depression, school refusal or expulsion, running away, trouble with the law, or trauma. Many have already tried outpatient therapy, day treatment or a short residential stay.

about_blocks.text: Treatment moves through four phases. It starts with the Outdoor Leadership Experience, six to eight weeks living and travelling in small groups in Algonquin Park. Students then move to the residence on campus, followed by a transition phase that splits time between campus and home, and finally aftercare at home. There is no fixed length of stay. Students move on when they are ready, and the centre gives the average as 12 to 14 months.

about_blocks.text: School continues the whole time. Certified teachers from the Upper Grand District School Board, all with special education qualifications, teach on campus, and most students work toward an Ontario Secondary School Diploma or Certificate. Parents are expected to take part as well, through family therapy, parent groups, retreats and workshops. Pine River calls this the Parallel Process, and its own outcome data links stronger parent involvement with better results after discharge.

about_blocks.text: Pine River receives funding support from the Ontario Ministry of Health. For Ontario adolescents who qualify for a funded bed, families pay a monthly fee of $325 toward costs the government funding does not cover. A small number of private-pay beds are available at $475 a day, and bursaries are offered to families who cannot afford the fees. Pine River is Accredited with Commendation by Accreditation Canada.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Pine River Institute

faqs.question: Who is Pine River Institute for?

answer_blocks.text: Pine River is for young people aged 13 to 19 with addictive behaviours, usually alongside other mental health issues such as anxiety, depression, self-harm or trauma. Most have already tried less intensive help, like outpatient therapy or day treatment, without enough progress. The admissions team decides with each family whether the program is the right fit.

Most have already tried less intensive help, like outpatient therapy or day treatment, without enough progress. The admissions team decides with each family whether the program is the right fit.

faqs.question: How much does Pine River Institute cost?

answer_blocks.text: For an Ontario teen who qualifies for a Ministry of Health funded bed, the family pays $325 a month plus a $1,000 damage deposit and trust account at admission. Private-pay beds cost $475 a day, with $17,750 due at admission. Aftercare is $325 a month, and the centre offers bursaries to families who cannot afford the fees.

faqs.question: Is Pine River funded by the Ontario government?

answer_blocks.text: Partly. Pine River describes itself as a not-for-profit, fee-for-service program that receives funding support from the Ontario Ministry of Health. The Ministry funds beds for Ontario adolescents who qualify, and families cover a monthly fee for things like parent retreats, transportation and activities. A limited number of beds are not Ministry funded and are paid privately.

faqs.question: How long does the program last?

answer_blocks.text: There is no set length of stay, and Pine River says the average is 12 to 14 months. Students move through the four phases when they show they are ready, not after a fixed number of days. Aftercare at home then lasts from three to 12 months, depending on the family.

faqs.question: What is the Outdoor Leadership Experience?

answer_blocks.text: It is the first phase of the program, six to eight weeks on the land in Algonquin Park. Groups of up to eight students and three staff canoe, hike or snowshoe, and do group work, individual therapy and journaling. After that, students move to the residence on the Shelburne-area campus.

faqs.question: Will my child keep up with school?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Certified teachers and an educational assistant from the Upper Grand District School Board teach on campus, and every teacher holds special education qualifications. Each student gets an academic plan, and most work toward an Ontario Secondary School Diploma or Certificate, while some take online post-secondary courses.

answer_blocks.text: Parents are expected to take an active part. That means regular family therapy and progress meetings, a family group every other Sunday, a parent group every two weeks in the evening, a parent retreat and two-day parent workshops twice a year. Families who live far away can join by phone or video, and each family has a private Family Bridge website to stay in touch.

faqs.question: Where is Pine River Institute and how far is it from Toronto?

answer_blocks.text: The campus is at 606060 River Road in Mulmur, just outside Shelburne in Dufferin County, about an hour and a half north of Toronto by car. Orangeville is about half an hour away, and Barrie and Collingwood are each about an hour. The head office is in downtown Toronto at 180 Dundas Street West, Suite 1410.

faqs.question: Does Pine River Institute offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: Pine River does not list medical detox among its services, and its recovery.com profile marks detox as not offered. The program is long-term residential treatment for teens. If your child may need medical withdrawal care first, ask the admissions team how they handle it before admission.

faqs.question: How do we apply, and is there a wait?

answer_blocks.text: Start with the online initial screener on Pine River's website, which takes about 10 minutes, or call admissions at 519-925-9225 ext. 139. If the fit looks right, you send supporting documents, your family may be placed on a wait list, and you visit the campus for an assessment before admission. The centre says the wait list can be months long, so it runs a six-week online support program for caregivers who are waiting.

faqs.question: What happens after my child leaves campus?

answer_blocks.text: Students and families build an Aftercare Plan during the transition phase, then continue with aftercare at home for three to 12 months. It includes individual, group and family therapy, weekly groups for students and for parents, and coaching. Aftercare ends with a graduation on campus.
